 VinFast VF MPV 7 Gets Massive Rs 4.10 Lakh Price Cut! 
 VinFast VF MPV 7 Gets Massive Rs 4.10 Lakh Price Cut!
 Written By: Kailash Jha Published: November 4, 2026 at 01:13 PM Updated: November 4, 2026 at 01:13 PM VinFast has reduced the ex-showroom price of its seven-seat VF MPV 7 from Rs 24.49 lakh to Rs 20.39 lakh, making it Rs 4.10 lakh cheaper. The revised price is listed on the company's official India website, while dealers are also promoting a separate festive benefit of Rs 40,780, subject to conditions. This puts the electric MPV much closer to the higher variants of the Kia Carens Clavis EV.
 The VF MPV 7 was launched in April 2026 as VinFast's first passenger-oriented electric MPV. It is offered in one variant with a 60.13kWh battery and seven seats. Buyers should distinguish the new listed ex-showroom price from any additional festival promotion, finance benefit or exchange incentive. They should also confirm when the offer ends and whether it applies to the colour and stock they want.
 How Much Cheaper Is The VF MPV 7?
 The earlier ex-showroom price of Rs 24,49,000 has come down to Rs 20,39,000. That is a straight difference of Rs 4,10,000, before considering registration, insurance, accessories and charging equipment. Some VinFast advertising mentions an additional festive benefit of Rs 40,780, which would increase the potential savings for an eligible customer. But that extra amount is not part of the standard listed price, and the applicable terms need checking at the dealership.
 Image: Screenshot from the Vinfast India website 
 The reduction changes its comparison with the Kia Carens Clavis EV. The Kia's electric range starts at around Rs 18 lakh and extends to about Rs 25 lakh, depending on battery and variant. At its former Rs 24.49 lakh price, the VinFast sat close to the most expensive Clavis EV. At Rs 20.39 lakh, it moves into a more competitive price bracket while retaining its larger battery.
 The BYD eMax 7 is another seven-seat electric alternative, with prices previously listed from Rs 26.90 lakh. It remains substantially more expensive than the revised VinFast. However, buyers should not compare the cheapest model in one range with a heavily equipped variant in another without checking seats, safety equipment, battery size and final on-road price.
 60.13kWh Battery, 517km Claimed Range
 The VF MPV 7 has a front-mounted electric motor producing 150kW, or approximately 204PS, and 280Nm. It drives the front wheels and has selectable Eco, Normal and Sport modes, along with adjustable regenerative braking. VinFast quotes an ARAI-certified range of 517km, but actual highway and city range will depend on load, speed, air-conditioning and driving conditions.
 DC charging is supported at up to 80kW, with a claimed 10–70% charge time of about 30 minutes using suitable equipment. That does not mean a full charge takes half an hour, or that every public charger can deliver 80kW. Charging access remains a practical consideration for a family vehicle intended for long journeys.
 How Practical Is It As A Family MPV?
 The vehicle measures 4,740mm long and has a 2,840mm wheelbase. The seating layout is 2+3+2, with sliding and reclining second-row seats. The third row also reclines. With all seven seats occupied, however, the boot holds only 126 litres. Folding the rear seats expands the available luggage space to a claimed 1,240 litres.
 Equipment includes a 10.1-inch touchscreen, Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, automatic climate control, rear air-conditioning controls, 19-inch alloy wheels and an electronic parking brake with auto hold. Safety features include four airbags, electronic stability control, traction control, hill-start assist and disc brakes on all four wheels. A Bharat NCAP crash-test result has not yet been published for this model.
 VinFast offers a seven-year vehicle warranty, ten-year battery warranty and three years of free maintenance under its stated ownership programme. It has also advertised free charging through the V-Green network until March 2029, subject to the programme's terms. Prospective buyers should verify network coverage in their city before treating that as a cash saving.
 The Rs 4.10 lakh reduction makes the VF MPV 7 much easier to consider, but it does not settle the purchase decision by itself. The real test will be third-row comfort, boot space with seven people aboard, charging convenience and confidence in local aftersales support. Those are the details that matter more than the size of a festive price cut.
